text_to_speech: are we alone in the universe is one of the fundamental questions of our time and involves a really interdisciplinary scientific approach as a microbiologist I'm interested understanding how microbes live in extreme environments for example hot pools and glacial environments so using a combination of field work and also laboratory based experiments I try to understand the limits of life and also identifying molecules that could be used as signatures of life now this is a really important because it could be used to understand that the fundamentals of life itself how life evolved on early Earth and how microbes can adapt to live in these environments it also has a bio technological perspective so some of these enzymes have a could be used from these environments for example in washing powder the information can be used to feed directly into interpreting data or form life detection missions for example this is really timely at the moment with Mars 2020 and ExoMars planned for for early next year I've recently been awarded 6.7 million by research England and we're going to use that money to kind of develop the area and kind of go past those additional boundaries of science and start looking it from this from an ethical and governor's perspective as well
